title: Vishal Mega Mart Ltd - 544307 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Vishal Mega Mart Q2 FY27 revenue rose 14% to INR3,399 crore, but same-store sales growth slowed to 5.4% as festivals shifted into Q3.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations grew 14% YoY to INR3,399 crore in Q2 FY27, with same-store sales growth (SSSG) of 5.4%, which management says would have been about 9% without the festival shift. Operating EBITDA rose 3.7% to INR262 crore, but margin fell to 7.7% from 8.5% on operating deleverage from low fixed-cost absorption. Adjusted PAT grew 6.4% to INR172 crore, with margin at 5.1% versus 5.4%. Store network reached 844 with 26 gross additions in the quarter, and management said it sees no demand moderation despite inflation.

financial_highlights.change: About 9% adjusted for festival shift (3-4pt impact)

financial_highlights.metric: Adjusted PAT (Q2 FY27, after ESOP charges)

financial_highlights.change: About 9.5% adjusted for festival shift (1.5-2pt impact)

financial_highlights.metric: Adjusted PAT (H1 FY27, after ESOP charges)
financial_highlights.change: +15.8% YoY; margin down from 6.2% (corrected on call from 6.4%)

financial_highlights.metric: Private brands share of revenue (H1 FY27)

financial_highlights.change: 26 gross adds in Q2; 53 in H1

segments.name: Large format stores (~18,000 sq ft)
segments.commentary: Core format; management sees room for about 2,000 large-format stores against roughly 850 today, and is prioritising these in all states. 24 of 26 Q2 openings were in Tier 2/3 towns.

segments.name: Small format stores (UP and Haryana pilot)
segments.commentary: 18 small-format stores now, with 2 added in Q2. Management sees potential for upwards of 3,000 stores nationally, but will open them only where large-format opportunity diminishes.

segments.name: Belong & Co. (apparel format)
segments.commentary: First pilot store launched in Q2 targeting young affluent urban shoppers. Management reports footfall-to-purchase conversion above 50% but says it is still learning and has not set a rollout plan.

segments.name: Quick commerce
segments.commentary: Expanded to 781 stores across 532 cities, with over 1.5 crore registered users. Management is increasing advertising and digital spend, starting in Delhi.

guidance_outlook: Management aims for double-digit SSSG for full FY27; Q3 SSSG must be above 10% for the nine months to look double-digit, per the analyst's arithmetic that management accepted.

Gross margin expected to hold YoY in Q3 and Q4 with no material impact from vendor price increases, supported by cost re-engineering; Q2 gross margin was down 30 bps, of which 20 bps came from apparel shift to Q3.
More than 100 new stores targeted for FY27, with the aim of beating the prior year's count every year.
EBITDA margin expected to improve about 30 bps a year over time, assuming double-digit growth against 6-7% store-level cost inflation.
No further price increases planned at the current inflation level, including after the festive season.
Employee cost pressure to ease: management says 8-10% SSSG is enough to offset the higher employee cost from minimum wage increases and new stores.
capex_capacity: Store additions: 26 gross in Q2 and 53 in H1 FY27; total 844 stores. Q2 split: 15 South (6 in Kerala, which now has 35 stores), 5 North, 4 East, 2 Western.
Management said the Kerala store plan was roughly doubled from the original estimate, with smaller stores, because the state is contiguous with no gaps between cities.
Large pilot in Gujarat and Maharashtra with smaller-format stores based on a hypothesis that higher affluence supports higher revenue per sq ft; management called it too early to conclude.
A fully automated large warehouse has been commissioned in North India, with plans for East, then South, then West warehouses.
Retail trading area is 1.41 crore sq ft. Area growth has trailed store growth; management said store size is set by catchment and that it solves for stores first.
demand_pricing: Management said demand is steady with no moderation; Q2 growth came mainly from market-share gain rather than existing customers buying more.
Price increases were taken mainly at higher price points. Opening price points had no increase and mid price points had very few changes.
Revenue mix: about 18-20% from opening price points, about 50% from mid, and about 24-25% from highest price points.
Rentals grew slowly versus area addition, which management attributed to Tier 2/3 expansion, not renegotiation. It expects this gap to continue.

Inventory days were around 65 in the base period versus 59-60 in H1 FY27 per an analyst's calculation; management attributed the gap to the festival shift, with the stock build happening three weeks later this year.
Weather and rainfall were uneven, causing one- to two-day revenue disruptions in some regions, but no regional demand weakness was reported.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 3-4% festive shift carry into Q3, and what Q3 SSSG is needed for a 9% first-half-equivalent?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed Q3 SSSG must be above 10% for the nine months to look double-digit, since festivals (Durga Puja, Dussehra, Navratri) moved from September to October.

qa_highlights.question: Will vendor price hikes hurt gross margin in Q3 and Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cost re-engineering has protected gross margin and vendors are already charging higher prices, so no material impact is expected in Q3 or Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost rise about INR10 crore QoQ, and what SSSG offsets the wage pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the rise reflects incremental ESOP cost and new stores, with minimum wage increases already in Q1. He said 8-10% SSSG is enough to offset the higher employee cost.

qa_highlights.question: How are price increases split across price points, and will there be more?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no further price increases are planned at the current inflation level, including after the festive season, and that opening price points were protected.

qa_highlights.question: How are new store openings split by region, and will Tier 1 entry follow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 24 of 26 Q2 openings were in Tier 2/3 towns and 15 were in South. It is piloting in Maharashtra and Gujarat, with stores in Ahmedabad, Surat, Pune and Baroda.

qa_highlights.question: How will the cash on the balance sheet be deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to more stores each year, Belong & Co. and small-format capacity, warehouses in East, South and West India, and quick commerce advertising. It said the board is still evaluating options.

risks_watch: Q3 SSSG must exceed 10% to deliver double-digit SSSG for the nine months; Q2 printed 5.4%.
Q2 EBITDA margin fell 80 bps YoY to 7.7% on deleverage; Q3 festive timing and fixed-cost absorption will decide whether H2 margins recover.
Employee cost is rising faster than revenue, with wage increases and new stores as drivers; the company says 8-10% SSSG is needed to offset it.
Inflation in raw materials and crude; management says gross margin will hold but pricing is frozen, which could limit flexibility.
Belong & Co. and small-format rollout are still at pilot stage; management has not set targets for Belong & Co.
Capital allocation of a large cash balance is under board review, with no decision yet.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and gross margin, saying there is no moderation and no further pricing plans. Guarded on Belong & Co. (still learning) and cash deployment (board review ongoing). Some evasiveness when pressed on the employee cost and margin trajectory, with the answer centred on store-count ambition.
key_quotes: Our goal is to achieve double-digit for the full year.
I'm absolutely committed to protecting our opening price points.
We would not want to inflate our gross margin.
Anything between 8% to 10% is good enough to offset this impact.

adds.what: Large-format stores (~18,000 sq ft) toward ~2,000 potential; 100+ new stores targeted for FY27 (53 opened in H1, 26 in Q2)
Fully automated large warehouse commissioned in North India; East, South, West warehouses planned next
Small-format stores (UP and Haryana pilot), 18 stores now, potential 3,000+ nationally, rollout conditional

growth.why: Management targets double-digit full-year SSSG (Q2 was 5.4%, ~9% festival-adjusted, requiring Q3 above 10%) and 100+ store openings in FY27, backed by 53 H1 openings and a commissioned North India warehouse, but no specific capacity or order numbers beyond store counts, and the EBITDA margin still fell to 7.7%.
